spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: Causality appears as analytic half-plane control: ordering one integration limit produces an i-epsilon Cauchy transform whose singularities lie below the real energy axis.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: The ordered kernel Sf,g is rewritten using Fourier transforms as a principal-value expression and then as a Cauchy integral with E'-E-i epsilon in the denominator. For suitable transformed boundary functions it is analytic in the upper half-plane; the source states that the resulting Jost function has zeros only on the real axis or in the lower half-plane.
directed.conceptual_reading: Temporal or causal ordering is converted into a geometric restriction on complex spectral data. This analytic asymmetry is the feature needed to rule out growing upper-half-plane modes within the model.
directed.representation_or_bridge: The distribution identity for the half-line ordered integral bridges dynamics in q-space to Hardy-type analyticity in energy.
directed.boundary_or_failure: The zero-location argument is only referred to earlier work and uses a finite-interval regularization. Good behavior of the Fourier data is assumed.
directed.uncertainty: Principal-value signs and the i-epsilon convention require scan verification; the prose claim about upper-half-plane analyticity is supported.
